<parameter name="content"># User Data Export: Implementation Tasks

Approved plan: build an API endpoint that exports all of a user's data. Use whatever format is easiest. Should be fast. Ship next week.

Defaults chosen so work can start now (each is a task below, not a re-open of the plan):
- Format: JSON (easiest, widely consumable)
- "Fast": stream the response / run as a background job if the export is large
- Target: ship next week

## 1. Discovery (day 1)
- [ ] 1.1 Inventory every table/store holding user data (DB tables, file/blob storage, third-party services, logs) and list what counts as "all of a user's data"
- [ ] 1.2 Identify fields that must be excluded or redacted (password hashes, tokens, internal flags, other users' data referenced by this user's records)
- [ ] 1.3 Record the inventory in the repo so reviewers can confirm completeness

## 2. API design (day 1)
- [ ] 2.1 Define the endpoint, e.g. `GET /api/users/me/export` (auth'd user exports only their own data)
- [ ] 2.2 Define the JSON schema: top-level object keyed by data category, with a `schema_version` and `exported_at`
- [ ] 2.3 Define error responses (401, 403, 429, 500)

## 3. Core implementation (days 2-3)
- [ ] 3.1 Add route and handler with authentication; derive the user ID from the session/token, never from a request parameter
- [ ] 3.2 Write one exporter function per data category, each returning serializable data
- [ ] 3.3 Aggregate exporters into the response; fetch categories in parallel where independent
- [ ] 3.4 Apply the redaction/exclusion rules from 1.2
- [ ] 3.5 Serialize to JSON, streaming the response so memory stays bounded for large accounts

## 4. Performance (day 3)
- [ ] 4.1 Avoid N+1 queries; use batched or joined queries per category
- [ ] 4.2 Paginate/stream large collections (messages, events, uploads) within the export
- [ ] 4.3 Set a target (e.g. p95 under a few seconds for a typical account) and measure against a large seeded account
- [ ] 4.4 If the target is missed, fall back to an async job: request returns a job ID, file is produced in the background, user downloads via a time-limited link

## 5. Security and abuse protection (day 3-4)
- [ ] 5.1 Rate limit the endpoint (e.g. a few requests per user per hour)
- [ ] 5.2 Consider re-authentication or recent-login check for this sensitive endpoint
- [ ] 5.3 Audit-log each export request (user, time, IP)
- [ ] 5.4 Set `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Content-Disposition: attachment` headers
- [ ] 5.5 Verify no cross-user data leakage (see test 6.3)

## 6. Testing (days 4-5)
- [ ] 6.1 Unit tests for each exporter
- [ ] 6.2 Integration test: full export for a seeded user matches the expected JSON
- [ ] 6.3 Authorization tests: unauthenticated rejected; user A cannot export user B's data
- [ ] 6.4 Test an empty account and a very large account
- [ ] 6.5 Test redaction: excluded fields never appear in output
- [ ] 6.6 Load test with concurrent exports

## 7. Docs and release (days 5-6)
- [ ] 7.1 Document the endpoint and JSON schema (API docs)
- [ ] 7.2 Add a feature flag for gradual rollout
- [ ] 7.3 Add monitoring: latency, error rate, export size, rate-limit hits
- [ ] 7.4 Deploy to staging and run a smoke test with a real-shaped account
- [ ] 7.5 Release to production behind the flag, then ramp up

## Items to confirm in parallel (do not block start)
- Whether legal/privacy requirements (e.g. GDPR/CCPA access requests) set a required scope or format; JSON generally satisfies "machine-readable"
- Whether the export should be delivered via the UI (download button) or API only for this release
